results.title: Continuity of recurrence coefficients and Gauss rules under convergence of moments
results.informal: If measures $\mu_N$ and $\mu$ on $[a,b]$ satisfy $\int p\,d\mu_N\to\int p\,d\mu$ for every polynomial and $\mu$ has more than $n$ support points, then $\alpha_k(\mu_N)\to\alpha_k(\mu)$, $\beta_k(\mu_N)\to\beta_k(\mu)$ for $k<n$, $\pi_n(\cdot;\mu_N)\to\pi_n(\cdot;\mu)$ uniformly on $[a,b]$, and the $n$-point Gauss nodes and weights converge.
hypotheses: The measures $\mu_N$ and $\mu$ are finite positive real measures with the required polynomial moments (in particular finite positive measures supported on a fixed compact interval).
For every $0\le k<2n$, the actual monomial moments $\int t^k\,d\mu_N$ converge to $\int t^k\,d\mu$.
The limiting support contains at least $n$ points. Early approximating Hankel systems may be singular; positivity is derived eventually from the limiting condition.
results.conclusion: The actual monic polynomials through degree $n$, squared norms and monic recurrence coefficients below $n$, canonically ordered $n$-point Gauss nodes, and original-measure integrated-cardinal weights converge. The polynomials converge uniformly on every bounded real set; Hankel systems are eventually positive definite and Jacobi matrices converge in spectral distance.
results.notes: Consumers: spectral-density estimation (averaged/limiting spectral measures, SLQ vs KPM), stability of Lanczos coefficients under perturbation of the moments. Prove.

results.informal: For a finite positive measure supported in $[a,b]$, a Gauss rule of order $n$, and $f$ holomorphic on a neighborhood of a positively oriented Jordan contour $\Gamma$ and its closed interior containing $[a,b]$, $R_n^G(f)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\oint_\Gamma K_n(z)f(z)\,dz$, where $K_n=\rho_n/\pi_n$ and $\rho_n(z)=\int\pi_n(t)/(z-t)\,d\mu(t)$. Consequently $|R_n^G(f)|\le\ell(\Gamma)\max_\Gamma|K_n|\max_\Gamma|f|/(2\pi)$. A null-homologous cycle with winding one on the support is an alternative domain hypothesis.
hypotheses: $\mu$ is a finite positive measure supported in $[a,b]$, and the canonical $n$-node Gauss rule exists up to its support termination threshold.

results.informal: For fixed polynomial coordinates $m_k=L(b_k)$ on $\mathcal P_{2n-1}$, with dual coefficients $c_k[p]$, let $\Phi(m)=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{n-1},L(1),\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{n-1})$. On the domain where the order-$n$ Gram matrix is positive definite, $\partial_{m_k}L(q)=c_k[q]+L(\partial_{m_k}q)$, $\dot\pi_j=-\sum_{i<j}\dot L(\pi_j\pi_i)\pi_i/h_i$, and $\dot h_j=\dot L(\pi_j^2)$. For $1\le j<n$, $\partial_{m_k}\beta_j=c_k[\Psi_{2j}]$ with $\Psi_{2j}=\beta_j(\pi_j^2/h_j-\pi_{j-1}^2/h_{j-1})$. For $0\le j<n$, $\partial_{m_k}\alpha_j=c_k[\Psi_{2j+1}]$ with $\Psi_{2j+1}=((t-\alpha_j)\pi_j^2-2\beta_j\pi_{j-1}\pi_j)/h_j$, omitting the preceding term at $j=0$. The mass row is $c_k[1]$. The absolute local condition number is the spectral norm of this Jacobian; the relative one multiplies by $\|m\|/\|\Phi(m)\|$ when the output normalization is nonzero.
hypotheses: $n\ge1$ and $b_0,\ldots,b_{2n-1}$ are a fixed basis of $\mathcal P_{2n-1}$, independent of $m$, with fixed dual coordinate functionals $c_k$.
The Gram matrix of $L$ on $\mathcal P_{n-1}$ is positive definite. This finite open domain supplies differentiability without nearby representing measures.
$h_j=L(\pi_j^2)$; $\beta_j=h_j/h_{j-1}$ for $j>0$, while the output mass $L(1)$ is distinct from the zero order recurrence boundary.
results.conclusion: The actual alpha-then-mass-and-beta map has the displayed coordinate Jacobian and absolute/relative Euclidean condition numbers. The highest requested alpha is expressed monically and uses only moments through degree $2n-1$.

results.title: Absolute and relative condition numbers of a differentiable map
results.informal:
For $f:\mathbb R^m	o\mathbb R^n$ Fréchet differentiable at $x$: $\operatorname{cond}_{abs}f(x)=\|Df(x)\|$. With nonzero input/output coordinates, componentwise relative conditioning is $\|D_{f(x)}^{-1}Df(x)D_x\|$, with entries $C_{
u\mu}=x_\mu\partial_\mu f_
u(x)/f_
u(x)$. Normwise relative conditioning is $\|Df(x)\|\|x\|/\|f(x)\|$ for nonzero input/output norms. Scalar formulas are $|f'(x)|$ and $|xf'(x)/f(x)|$. For an invertible linear map, only the normwise relative quantity is bounded by $\kappa(A)$; the componentwise relative quantity has the separate bound $\|D_{f(x)}^{-1}\|\|Df(x)\|\|D_x\|$.
hypotheses: $f$ Fréchet differentiable at $x$; Euclidean norms for the matrix coordinate formulas
nonzero input/output coordinates for componentwise relative interpretation; nonzero input/output norms for normwise relative interpretation
results.conclusion: absolute, normwise relative and componentwise relative condition definitions, scalar formulas, the normwise linear-map bound by $\kappa(A)$, and the componentwise diagonal-scaling bound
results.notes: NLAlib has only the matrix condition number. Consumers: `recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity`, perturbation statements in matrix-conditioning. Prove (definitions). Statement correction (frontier derivations, psd:map-condition): distinguish relative perturbation metrics. An orthogonal Hadamard 2x2 matrix has kappa=1, but at x=(1,1+epsilon) its second coordinate-relative derivative row is (-1/epsilon,(1+epsilon)/epsilon), unbounded as epsilon decreases to zero. A matrix-condition-number bound alone therefore cannot control the componentwise Euclidean metric.

results.title: Modified Chebyshev algorithm: Jacobi matrix from modified moments
results.informal: Given monic $p_k$ with $p_{k+1}=(t-a_k)p_k-b_kp_{k-1}$ and modified moments $m_k=\int p_k\,d\mu$ ($k<2n$), the mixed moments $\sigma_{kl}=\int\pi_kp_l\,d\mu$ satisfy $\sigma_{-1,l}=0$, $\sigma_{0,l}=m_l$, $\sigma_{kl}=\sigma_{k-1,l+1}-(\alpha_{k-1}-a_l)\sigma_{k-1,l}-\beta_{k-1}\sigma_{k-2,l}+b_l\sigma_{k-1,l-1}$, and $\alpha_0=a_0+m_1/m_0$, $\alpha_k=a_k-\sigma_{k-1,k}/\sigma_{k-1,k-1}+\sigma_{k,k+1}/\sigma_{kk}$, $\beta_k=\sigma_{kk}/\sigma_{k-1,k-1}$, $\beta_0=m_0$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ positive with more than $n$ support points
$p_k$ monic with a known three-term recurrence ($a_k\in\mathbb R$, $b_k\ge0$)

results.title: Christoffel and Uvarov theorems: orthogonal polynomials of rationally modified measures
results.informal: For $d\hat\mu=(u/v)\,d\mu$ with $u,v$ coprime real polynomials with simple zeros, not vanishing on the support, $u\hat\pi_n$ is (up to a constant) the determinant with first row $\pi_{n-m},\dots,\pi_{n+\ell}$ ($\ell=\deg u$, $m=\deg v\le n$), rows of values $\pi_j(u_i)$ at the zeros of $u$ and rows of Cauchy integrals $\rho_j(v_i)$ at the zeros of $v$; a bordered variant holds for $m>n$. Special cases give the linear/quadratic factor and divisor algorithms, e.g. $\hat\pi_n=\pi_n+s_n\pi_{n-1}+t_n\pi_{n-2}$ for a quadratic divisor.
hypotheses: The measure specialization uses a finite positive real measure $\mu$ supported in $[a,b]$, so compact support and a pole-free denominator give the required divided polynomial moments. Compact support alone does not imply finite mass.

In the measure specialization $u,v$ are nonzero real polynomials, $v$ has no zero on $[a,b]$, and $u/v>0$ there. The traditional root presentation assumes coprime polynomials with simple exterior roots; the coefficient/remainder construction also permits repeated roots and common factors.

The generic coefficient/determinant branch uses a polynomial functional over a scalar field and the actual finite nonsingular modified Hankel system at the requested order; it does not require a finite measure or positivity. The compressed original-basis formulas additionally require the finite original orthogonality systems actually used.
results.conclusion: determinantal formulas for $u\,\pi_n(\cdot;\hat\mu)$; recurrence coefficients of $\hat\mu$ computable from those of $\mu$ and $\rho_k$.
results.notes: Consumers: spectral measures modified by resolvents ($(t-z)^{-1}d\mu_b$: shifted systems, rational Krylov), Gauss rules for $f(t)/(t-z)$. Assume or prove the linear cases first.

results.title: Schur triangularization, real Schur form and Schur's inequality
results.informal: Every $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ is $A=UTU^*$ with $U$ unitary and $T$ upper triangular, the eigenvalues on the diagonal in any prescribed order; a real $A$ is $A=QTQ^\top$ with $Q$ real orthogonal and $T$ real upper quasitriangular ($1\times1$ real blocks and general $2\times2$ real blocks for conjugate eigenvalue pairs), and $T$ can be taken triangular when all eigenvalues are real. Consequences: Schur's inequality $\sum_i|\lambda_i|^2=\|A\|_F^2-\|N\|_F^2\le\|A\|_F^2$ ($N$ the strictly upper part, equality iff $A$ normal); matrices with distinct eigenvalues are dense; over $\mathbb C$, over $\mathbb C$, for every $\varepsilon>0$ some similarity makes $A$ triangular with off-diagonal entries at most $\varepsilon$. Pencil version (QZ): $A=VT_AW^*$, $B=VT_BW^*$ simultaneously.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ (real Schur form) or $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ (complex Schur form)
prescribed ordering of the eigenvalues for the complex form
results.conclusion: $\exists$ orthogonal $Q$ (unitary $U$), quasitriangular (triangular) $T$: $A=QTQ^\top$; $\sum|\lambda_i|^2\le\|A\|_F^2$ with equality iff $A$ is normal

A real normal matrix is real orthogonally similar to a direct sum of $1\times1$ blocks and $2\times2$ blocks $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix}$ (skew-symmetric and orthogonal matrices as special cases). Fuglede–Putnam: for normal $A,B$, $AX=XB\iff A^*X=XB^*$.

Geometric multiplicity $\ge k$ forces $\lambda$ into the spectrum of every principal submatrix of order $\ge n-k+1$, hence algebraic multiplicity $\ge k$.

Simultaneous triangularization by similarity is equivalent to unitary simultaneous triangularization.

results.title: CS decomposition of a partitioned unitary matrix and canonical form of an oblique projection

results.informal: If $U=\begin{pmatrix}U_{11}&U_{12}\\U_{21}&U_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ is unitary (real orthogonal) with $U_{11}\in\mathbb C^{p\times p}$, $p\le q$, there are unitaries $V_1,W_1\in\mathbb C^{p\times p}$, $V_2,W_2\in\mathbb C^{q\times q}$ with $(V_1\oplus V_2)^*U(W_1\oplus W_2)=\begin{pmatrix}C&S&0\\-S&C&0\\0&0&I_{q-p}\end{pmatrix}$, $C=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i(U_{11}))$, $S=(I-C^2)^{1/2}$. In particular $\operatorname{rank}U_{12}=\operatorname{rank}U_{21}$ and $\operatorname{rank}U_{22}=\operatorname{rank}U_{11}+n-2p$. An idempotent $P$ with singular values $\sigma_1\ge\dots\ge\sigma_g>1$ is unitarily similar to $\bigoplus_i\begin{pmatrix}1&(\sigma_i^2-1)^{1/2}\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\oplus I\oplus0$, so, when $\operatorname{rank}P>0$, $\|P\|=1/\cos\theta_{\max}$ between its range and the orthogonal complement of its null space.
hypotheses: $U\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ orthogonal, partitioned with $U_{11}\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, $p\le n-p$
for the projection form: $P^2=P$
results.conclusion: block-orthogonal $V,W$ with $V^\top UW$ in CS form; $\operatorname{rank}U_{12}=\operatorname{rank}U_{21}$; for idempotent $P$, $\|P\|=\sigma_1(P)$ is the secant of the largest principal angle
results.notes: Consumers: principal-angles-def (CSD is the canonical form behind sin Θ/cos Θ), davis-kahan-sin-theta, wedin-sin-theta, oblique projectors in Nyström / generalized Nyström and sketch-and-solve-ls analyses (‖P‖ = ‖I − P‖ = 1/cos θ at proper positive rank), subspace-iteration-convergence. The secant formula needs positive projection rank; ‖P‖=‖I−P‖ requires both range and kernel to have positive dimension. The formalization treats zero, full and empty ranks separately.

If $B$ has $\pi$ positive and $\nu$ negative eigenvalues then $\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+\pi}(A)$ and $\lambda_{i-\nu}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)$. In particular if $\operatorname{rank}B=r$ then $\lambda_{i-r}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+r}(A)$, and for $z\in\mathbb R^n$: $\lambda_i(A)\le\lambda_i(A+zz^\top)\le\lambda_{i+1}(A)$ and $\lambda_{i-1}(A)\le\lambda_i(A-zz^\top)\le\lambda_i(A)$.
hypotheses: $A=A^\top$, $B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$
$\pi=\#\{\lambda_j(B)>0\}$, $\nu=\#\{\lambda_j(B)<0\}$ (or $\operatorname{rank}B=r$)

results.conclusion: $\lambda_{i-\nu}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+\pi}(A)$; rank-one interlacing for $A\pm zz^\top$
results.notes: Consumers: Nyström and low-rank-plus-residual analyses ($A-\hat A$ has rank $\le n-k$ perturbation structure), `partial-cholesky-nystrom` (each pivot step is a rank-one downdate), deflation in `subspace-iteration-convergence`, and eigenvalue counting in `sylvester-inertia`. results.title: Eigenvalues of the Hermitian part majorize the real parts of the eigenvalues
results.informal: For $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with eigenvalues $z_i$ and Hermitian part $H(A)=(A+A^*)/2$, the vector $\lambda(H(A))$ majorizes $(\operatorname{Re}z_i)$; conversely every such pair $x\succ\operatorname{Re}z$ is realised by some $A$. Corollary (Bendixson): $\lambda_{\min}(H(A))\le\operatorname{Re}z_i\le\lambda_{\max}(H(A))$.

results.title: Ostrowski's theorem: eigenvalues under congruence
results.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with singular values $\sigma_1\ge\dots\ge\sigma_n$, for each $k$ there is $\theta_k\in[\sigma_n^2,\sigma_1^2]$ with $\lambda_k(SAS^\top)=\theta_k\lambda_k(A)$ (same ordering). Hence $\sigma_n^2\lambda_k(A)\le\lambda_k(SAS^\top)\le\sigma_1^2\lambda_k(A)$ for $\lambda_k(A)\ge0$ (reversed for $\lambda_k(A)<0$), and $SAS^\top$ has no more positive (negative) eigenvalues than $A$.
hypotheses: $A=A^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$
$S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ (nonsingular for $\theta_k>0$)
results.conclusion: $\lambda_k(SAS^\top)=\theta_k\lambda_k(A)$ with $\sigma_n(S)^2\le\theta_k\le\sigma_1(S)^2$
results.notes: Consumers: eigenvalues of preconditioned or sketched Gram matrices $S A S^\top$ (`sketch-and-precondition`, `preconditioned-cg`, `nystrom-pcg`), quantitative inertia. Prove via Courant–Fischer: $x^\top SAS^\top x=y^\top Ay$ with $y=S^\top x$ and $\sigma_n^2\|x\|^2\le\|y\|^2\le\sigma_1^2\|x\|^2$.

results.title: Simultaneous diagonalisation of a definite pair by congruence
results.informal: If $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ is symmetric positive definite and $B$ symmetric, there is a nonsingular $S$ with $A=SS^\top$ and $B=S\Lambda S^\top$, $\Lambda$ real diagonal whose entries are the eigenvalues of $A^{-1}B$ (and $\Lambda$ has the inertia of $B$). Consequently $A^{-1}B$ (and $AB$) is diagonalisable with real eigenvalues, nonnegative if $B\succeq0$. More generally (Thm 4.5.17) for invertible symmetric $A$, $A,B$ are simultaneously congruent to real diagonals iff $A^{-1}B$ is diagonalisable with real spectrum. A PSD–PSD version holds with $A=S(I_r\oplus0)S^\top$.

results.title: Geršgorin refinements and diagonal dominance
results.informal: Let $R_i=\sum_{j\ne i}|a_{ij}|$, $C_j=\sum_{i\ne j}|a_{ij}|$. (i) A union of $k$ Geršgorin discs disjoint from the remaining $n-k$ contains exactly $k$ eigenvalues; the column discs work too. (ii) $\rho(A)\le\min\{\max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|,\max_j\sum_i|a_{ij}|\}$, and with positive weights $\rho(A)\le\max_ip_i^{-1}\sum_jp_j|a_{ij}|$. (iii) If $A$ is strictly diagonally dominant ($|a_{ii}|>R_i$) with positive diagonal, every eigenvalue has positive real part; if moreover $A$ is symmetric it is positive definite. (iv) Taussky: an irreducible weakly diagonally dominant matrix with at least one strictly dominant row is nonsingular (and PD if symmetric with positive diagonal).
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ (real symmetric for the PD conclusions)
results.conclusion: eigenvalue counts in isolated disc unions; row/column-sum spectral radius bounds; diagonal dominance ⇒ Re λ > 0 / PD

results.title: Bauer–Fike theorem and residual bounds for diagonalisable matrices
results.informal: Let $A=V\Lambda V^{-1}$ be diagonalisable and $E$ arbitrary. Every eigenvalue $\hat\lambda$ of $A+E$ satisfies $\min_i|\hat\lambda-\lambda_i|\le\kappa(V)\,|||E|||$ for any matrix norm induced by an absolute vector norm (e.g. $\|\cdot\|_1,\|\cdot\|_2,\|\cdot\|_\infty$), with $\kappa(V)=|||V|||\,|||V^{-1}|||$. If $A$ is normal, $\min_i|\hat\lambda-\lambda_i|\le\|E\|_2$. Residual form: for $\hat x\ne0$ and $r=A\hat x-\hat\lambda\hat x$, $\min_i|\hat\lambda-\lambda_i|\le\kappa(V)\|r\|/\|\hat x\|$ (and $\le\|r\|_2/\|\hat x\|_2$ for normal $A$).
hypotheses: $A=V\Lambda V^{-1}\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $\Lambda$ diagonal
$E\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$
norm induced by an absolute vector norm
results.conclusion: $\operatorname{dist}(\hat\lambda,\sigma(A))\le\kappa(V)|||E|||$; residual analogue
results.notes: Consumers: `gmres-diagonalizable` (the $\kappa(V)$ factor), `eigenvalue-residual-bounds` (normal case generalises its part (a)), eigenvalue sensitivity in `qr-algorithm-convergence`. Prove: if $\hat\lambda\notin\sigma(A)$ then $I+(\Lambda-\hat\lambda)^{-1}V^{-1}EV$ is singular, so $1\le\|(\Lambda-\hat\lambda)^{-1}\|\kappa(V)\|E\|$; spectral-norm case first (difficulty 2).

results.title: Sylvester's criterion for positive (semi)definiteness
results.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $A\succ0$ iff all nonempty leading principal minors are positive, equivalently all trailing ones; $A\succeq0$ iff all principal minors are nonnegative. If the first $n-1$ leading minors are positive and $\det A\ge0$, then $A\succeq0$. Writing $p_A(t)=\sum_j c_jt^j$, positive semidefiniteness is also equivalent to $(-1)^k c_{n-k}\ge0$ for every $0\le k\le n$, with zero coefficients retaining their degrees.
hypotheses: $A=A^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$
results.conclusion: PD iff positive leading or trailing minors; PSD iff all principal minors are nonnegative, or iff $(-1)^k p_A.\operatorname{coeff}(n-k)\ge0$ for every $k\le n$; the positive-proper-leading-minors boundary criterion
results.notes: Consumers: existence of LU/Cholesky without pivoting for SPD matrices (`lu-decomposition`, `cholesky-algorithm`), positivity of pivots in `rpcholesky` and `partial-cholesky-nystrom`, principal-minor arguments in `volume-sampling`. Prove the PD case by induction with `posDef_iff_pivotSchur` and `det_eq_mul_det_pivotSchur`; PSD case via $A+\varepsilon I$. Statement correction: signs in the characteristic coefficient test are assigned by degree, with zero coefficients allowed. Merely deleting zero coefficients and alternating the remaining signs is false: diag(1,-1) has characteristic polynomial X^2-1 but is not PSD, certified by NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_one_neg_one_eq and NLAlib.not_posSemidef_diagonal_one_neg_one. results.title: Matrices with positive (semi)definite Hermitian part
results.informal: Let $A=H+iK$ with $H,K$ Hermitian. If $H\succeq0$ then $\ker A\subseteq\ker H$, $\operatorname{rank}H\le\operatorname{rank}A$, and $A$ has the row/column inclusion property when the ranks agree (always when $H\succ0$). If $H\succ0$: $\det H\le|\det A|$ (Ostrowski–Taussky, equality iff $K=0$), $\det H+|\det K|\le|\det A|$ for $n\ge2$, and $(\det H)^{2/n}+|\det K|^{2/n}\le|\det A|^{2/n}$ (Fan).
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $H=(A+A^*)/2$, $K=(A-A^*)/(2i)$
$H\succeq0$ (resp. $H\succ0$)

results.title: Kantorovich and Wielandt inequalities
aliases: angle bound for positive definite forms
results.informal: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite with extreme eigenvalues $\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}$ and $\kappa=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}$. Kantorovich: $(x^\top Ax)(x^\top A^{-1}x)\le\frac{(\lambda_{\min}+\lambda_{\max})^2}{4\lambda_{\min}\lambda_{\max}}\|x\|^4=\tfrac14(\kappa^{1/2}+\kappa^{-1/2})^2\|x\|^4$. Wielandt: for orthogonal $x,y$, $(x^\top Ay)^2\le\big(\frac{\lambda_{\max}-\lambda_{\min}}{\lambda_{\max}+\lambda_{\min}}\big)^2(x^\top Ax)(y^\top Ay)$. The two inequalities are equivalent.

results.title: PSD block matrices: contractions, Schur complements and inverse principal submatrices
results.informal: For $X\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$: $\begin{bmatrix}I&X\\X^\top&I\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ ($\succ0$) iff $\|X\|\le1$ ($<1$). For $H=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^\top&C\end{bmatrix}$ with $A,C\succeq0$, TFAE: $H\succeq0$; $(x^\top Ax)(y^\top Cy)\ge(x^\top By)^2$ for all $x,y$; $x^\top Ax+y^\top Cy\ge2|x^\top By|$; $B=A^{1/2}XC^{1/2}$ with $\|X\|\le1$; if $A,C\succ0$ also $\rho(B^\top A^{-1}BC^{-1})\le1$ (strict versions characterise $H\succ0$, equivalently $A\succ0$ and $C-B^\top A^{-1}B\succ0$). For $A,B\succeq0$: $A\succeq B$ iff $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&A\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$. For $H\succ0$ and an index set $\alpha$: $(H^{-1})_{\alpha\alpha}\succeq(H_{\alpha\alpha})^{-1}$; $\begin{bmatrix}A&X\\X^\top&X^\top A^{-1}X\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ for $A\succ0$.
hypotheses: real symmetric block matrices
$A,C\succeq0$ (or $\succ0$ where stated)
results.conclusion: the listed equivalences and Loewner inequalities
results.notes: Consumers: Cauchy–Schwarz for PSD bilinear forms in approximate-matrix-multiplication and subspace-embedding proofs (`amm-ose`, `ose-def`), Nyström error via Schur complements (`nystrom-structural`, `generalized-schur-complement-psd`), inverse-diagonal lower bounds $(A^{-1})_{ii}\ge1/a_{ii}$ for diagonal estimation of $A^{-1}$ (`diagonal-estimator`), Hermitian dilation arguments. The singular contraction factorization follows from a block Gram square root and rectangular polar decompositions; the strict variants and inverse compression follow from the proved Schur and relative-spectrum interfaces. Strict test quantifiers: the product inequality is strict for x≠0 and y≠0; the absolute bilinear-sum inequality is strict for (x,y)≠(0,0). Weak tests include all zero vectors. The square-root contraction factorization includes singular PSD diagonal blocks and empty blocks.

results.title: Hadamard, Fischer, Koteljanskiĭ and Szász determinant inequalities
results.informal: For symmetric positive definite $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $\det A\le\prod_ia_{ii}$ with equality iff $A$ is diagonal for positive definite $A$; for PSD $A$, equality holds iff $A$ is diagonal or some diagonal entry is zero (Hadamard), hence $|\det B|\le\prod_j\|b_j\|_2$ for any square $B$ with columns $b_j$ (equality iff orthogonal columns or a zero column); $\det\begin{bmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{bmatrix}\le\det A_{11}\det A_{22}$ (Fischer); $\det A_{\alpha\cup\beta}\det A_{\alpha\cap\beta}\le\det A_\alpha\det A_\beta$ (Koteljanskiĭ); and the normalised products $P_k^{1/\binom{n-1}{k-1}}$ of $k\times k$ principal minors decrease in $k$ (Szász).
hypotheses: $A=A^\top\succ0$; determinant inequalities also hold for PSD input, with equality cases qualified separately.
$\alpha,\beta\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$
results.conclusion: the listed determinant inequalities with equality cases
results.notes: Consumers: `volume-sampling` and column subset selection (Gram determinants bounded by products of column norms; NLAlib already has the base-times-height identity `det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobSq_sub_projector`), `rpcholesky` / `partial-cholesky-nystrom` (determinants of pivot blocks), determinant bounds for random matrices. Prove Hadamard from Cholesky ($\det A=\prod L_{ii}^2$, `IsCholesky.det_eq_prod_sq`, with $L_{ii}^2\le a_{ii}$) or QR ($|\det B|=\prod|R_{ii}|\le\prod\|b_j\|$); Fischer from the Schur complement $A_{22}-A_{21}A_{11}^{-1}A_{12}\preceq A_{22}$; Koteljanskiĭ uses overlapping Schur blocks; Szász uses inverse-Hadamard, Jacobi deletion identities and finite subset incidence products. Equality in PSD Hadamard is diagonal structure or a zero diagonal entry. The Fischer, Koteljanski, and nontrivial Szász equality characterizations are stated on positive definite input; their PSD extensions assert the inequalities without importing those equality characterizations.

results.title: Lebesgue constant of Chebyshev truncation and near-best projection (ATAP Thms 15.1, 15.3, 16.1)
results.informal: The degree-$n$ Chebyshev truncation $f\mapsto f_n$ is a linear projection of $C[-1,1]$ onto $\mathcal P_n$ whose norm is the Dirichlet-kernel integral $\Lambda_n=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\left|\frac{\sin((n+\frac12)t)}{\sin(t/2)}\right|dt\le\frac4{\pi^2}\log(n+1)+3$. With the general near-best lemma $\|f-Lf\|\le(1+\|L\|)E_n(f)$ this gives $\|f-f_n\|\le(4+\frac4{\pi^2}\log(n+1))E_n(f)$.
hypotheses: $f$ continuous on $[-1,1]$, $n\ge1$
$f_n=\sum_{k\le n}a_k(f)T_k$ the Chebyshev truncation (chebyshev-coefficients-def)
for the lemma: $L$ linear on $C[-1,1]$ with $Lp=p$ for $\deg p\le n$ and $\|Lf\|_\infty\le\Lambda\|f\|_\infty$
results.conclusion: $\|f-Lf\|_\infty\le(1+\Lambda)E_n(f)$; $\max_{[-1,1]}|f_n|\le\Lambda_n\max_{[-1,1]}|f|$ with $\Lambda_n\le\frac4{\pi^2}\log(n+1)+3$; hence $\|f-f_n\|_\infty\le\big(4+\frac4{\pi^2}\log(n+1)\big)E_n(f)$

results.title: Lower bounds on Lebesgue constants; exponential growth for equispaced nodes (ATAP Thm 15.2)
results.informal: For any $n+1$ distinct nodes in $[-1,1]$ the interpolation Lebesgue constant satisfies $\Lambda_n\ge\frac2\pi\log(n+1)+0.52125\ldots$, and for equispaced nodes $\Lambda_n>2^{n-2}/n^2$ ($n\ge1$).

results.conclusion: $\Lambda_n\ge\frac2\pi(\log(n+1)+\gamma+\log\frac4\pi)$; for equispaced nodes and $n\ge1$, $\Lambda_n>2^n/(4n^2)$, equivalently $2^{n-2}/n^2$ with the real exponent interpreted correctly at $n=1$.
results.notes: The equispaced bound uses the full cardinal binomial sum at the first half-grid point; a single endpoint cardinal does not suffice. results.title: Roots of a Chebyshev series are colleague-matrix eigenvalues (ATAP Thm 18.1)
results.informal: For $p=\sum_{k=0}^na_kT_k$ with $a_n\ne0$, $\det(xI-C)=p(x)/(2^{n-1}a_n)$ for the colleague matrix $C$ (tridiagonal with $\frac12$ off the diagonal, first-row entry $1$, last row corrected by $-a_k/(2a_n)$); so its eigenvalues are the roots of $p$ with multiplicity.
hypotheses: $n\ge1$, $a_n\ne0$; $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ as in ATAP (18.1)
results.conclusion: $\operatorname{charpoly}C=\dfrac{1}{2^{n-1}a_n}\sum_{k=0}^na_kT_k$; in particular the eigenvalues of $C$ are the roots of $p$

mathlib_prereqs.note: No companion-matrix API in Mathlib; expand the determinant directly

results.notes: The proof identifies the actual Chebyshev quotient basis with multiplication by X in AdjoinRoot, so the characteristic polynomial is the monic normalization and multiplicities are retained. Degree one uses the scalar matrix [−a₀/a₁]; the printed half-off-diagonal row convention applies from degree two.

results.title: Chebyshev series of |x| and sign(x) (ATAP Ex 3.6, Bernstein 1914)
results.informal: $|x|=\frac2\pi+\frac4\pi\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{j+1}}{4j^2-1}T_{2j}(x)$ uniformly on $[-1,1]$, so the degree-$2m$ truncation has error $\le\frac{2}{\pi(2m+1)}$; and $\operatorname{sign}(x)=\frac4\pi\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{(-1)^j}{2j+1}T_{2j+1}(x)$ (convergence away from $0$).
results.conclusion: the Chebyshev coefficients of $|x|$ are $a_0=2/\pi$, $a_{2j}=\frac{4}{\pi}\frac{(-1)^{j+1}}{4j^2-1}$, $a_{2j+1}=0$; $\max_{[-1,1]}\big||x|-\sum_{k\le 2m}a_kT_k\big|\le\sum_{j>m}|a_{2j}|=\frac{2}{\pi(2m+1)}$; the coefficients of sign are $\frac4\pi\frac{(-1)^j}{2j+1}$ at $k=2j+1$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Fourier series machinery

results.notes: Consumers: sign-polynomial-approx and sign-approx-lower-bound (explicit $O(1/n)$ uniform approximation of $|x|$, the classical starting point for approximating sign and spectral projectors), abs-best-approx-asymptotics (upper half). The extracted ATAP text prints the sign coefficient as $(-1)^{k-1}$; use $(-1)^{(k-1)/2}$. Prove (cosine series of $|\cos\theta|$).

results.title: Chebyshev series of e^{ax}: modified Bessel coefficients (ATAP Ex 3.15)
results.informal: $e^{ax}=I_0(a)+2\sum_{k\ge1}I_k(a)T_k(x)$ uniformly on $[-1,1]$ with $I_k(a)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\pi e^{a\cos\theta}\cos k\theta\,d\theta$, and $0\le I_k(a)\le\frac{(a/2)^k}{k!}e^{a^2/4}$ for $a\ge0$; truncation at degree $n$ has error $\le2\sum_{k>n}|I_k(a)|$.
hypotheses: $a\in\mathbb R$, $x\in[-1,1]$
results.conclusion: the Chebyshev coefficients of $e^{ax}$ are $2I_k(a)$ ($I_0(a)$ for $k=0$), with the stated bound on $I_k$

results.title: Fejér: Cesàro means of Chebyshev series converge uniformly (ATAP Ex 6.6)
results.informal: For every $f\in C[-1,1]$ the Cesàro means $S_n=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{m=0}^nf_m$ of its Chebyshev truncations converge uniformly to $f$; $S_n=\sum_{k\le n}(1-\frac{k}{n+1})a_kT_k$ is a positive operator ($f\ge0\Rightarrow S_nf\ge0$) of norm $1$.
hypotheses: $f$ continuous on $[-1,1]$
results.conclusion: $S_nf\to f$ uniformly on $[-1,1]$; $\|S_nf\|_\infty\le\|f\|_\infty$ and $S_nf\ge0$ when $f\ge0$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Mathlib has Fourier series on AddCircle but no Fejér-mean convergence theorem

results.notes: Consumers: kernel polynomial method / Chebyshev-moment spectral-density estimation, where damping (Fejér or Jackson kernel) makes the approximant positive and the estimated density a probability measure; positivity-preserving polynomial approximation in trace estimation. Prove via the Fejér kernel on the circle.

results.title: Every best uniform approximant interpolates f at n+1 points (ATAP Ex 10.12)
results.informal: If $p^*$ is the best approximation of degree $\le n$ to real $f\in C[-1,1]$, there are $n+1$ distinct points $-1<x_0<\dots<x_n<1$ with $p^*(x_j)=f(x_j)$.
hypotheses: $f$ continuous and real on $[-1,1]$
$p^*$ attains $E_n(f)$ (minimax-error-def)
results.conclusion: $\exists\,x_0<\cdots<x_n$ in $(-1,1)$ with $f(x_j)=p^*(x_j)$; hence $p^*$ = `Lagrange.interpolate` of $f$ at these points
results.notes: Consumers: links best approximation to interpolation (lets Lebesgue-constant and interpolation-remainder bounds apply to $p^*$); Marcinkiewicz-type constructions. Immediate from equioscillation by the intermediate value theorem. Prove after equioscillation.

results.title: Rational best approximation: existence, uniqueness and equioscillation (ATAP Thm 24.1, Ex 24.5)
results.informal: A real $f\in C[-1,1]$ has a unique best real approximation $r^*\in R_{mn}$ (type $(m,n)$), and real $r\in R_{mn}$ is $r^*$ iff $f-r$ equioscillates at $\ge m+n+2-d$ points, $d=\min(m-\mu,n-\nu)$ the defect of $r$ of exact type $(\mu,\nu)$; if $f-r$ alternates in sign at $m+n+2-d$ points with $|f-r|\ge\varepsilon$ there, then $\|f-r^*\|\ge\varepsilon$.
hypotheses: $f$ real continuous on $[-1,1]$; $m,n\ge0$
$R_{mn}=\{p/q:\deg p\le m,\deg q\le n,\ q\ne0\text{ on }[-1,1]\}$
results.conclusion: existence and uniqueness of $r^*$; characterisation by $m+n+2-d$ alternation points; the de la Vallée Poussin lower bound

results.title: Best approximation of |x|: Bernstein's constant and Newman–Stahl rational rate (ATAP Thm 25.1)
results.informal: $E_{n,0}(|x|;[-1,1])\sim\beta/n$ with $\beta=0.2801\ldots$ and $E_{n,n}(|x|)\sim8e^{-\pi\sqrt n}$.
hypotheses: best uniform approximation errors on $[-1,1]$ by polynomials of degree $\le n$, resp. type $(n,n)$ rationals
results.conclusion: $nE_{n,0}(|x|)\to\beta$ and $E_{n,n}(|x|)e^{\pi\sqrt n}\to8$
results.notes: Consumers: sign-approx-lower-bound / sign-polynomial-approx (the polynomial rate for $|x|$ is $\Theta(1/n)$, so gap-free sign approximation cannot beat $1/n$; a non-asymptotic $E_{n,0}(|x|)\ge c/n$ is the useful part and follows from Bernstein-type arguments). Assume the asymptotics; prove only a non-asymptotic lower bound if a consumer needs it.

results.title: Independent Gaussian probes certify the spectral norm
results.informal: For a fixed real rectangular matrix $R$, $s\ge1$ independent standard Gaussian test vectors give the upper certificate $U=\alpha\sqrt{2/\pi}\max_{j\le s}\|Rg_j\|_2$ with $\mathbb P\{\|R\|_2>U\}\le\alpha^{-s}$.
hypotheses: $R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ is deterministic, $s\ge1$, and $\alpha>1$
$g_1,\ldots,g_s$ are mutually independent with law $N(0,I_n)$
results.conclusion: $\mathbb P\{\|R\|_2>\alpha\sqrt{2/\pi}\max_{j\le s}\|Rg_j\|_2\}\le\alpha^{-s}$
results.notes: Derivation checked: for R nonzero, project each probe onto a top right singular vector. The scalar normal density bound gives P(|Z|<t) <= sqrt(2/pi)*t; at t=sqrt(pi/2)/alpha independence yields alpha^(-s). R=0 and zero-dimensional matrices have empty failure events. The probes must be independent of the residual construction. This is a certificate for any residual operator, not a claim about a particular stopping algorithm. Formalization should use HasLaw and the actual maximum of finitely many probe norms.

results.title: Fresh-probe residual certificates remain valid under adaptive stopping
results.informal: At stage $t$, choose $R_t$ using the history $\mathcal F_t$, then draw $s_t$ fresh independent standard Gaussian probes. For deterministic $\alpha_t>1$ with $\sum_{t\ge0}\alpha_t^{-s_t}\le\delta$, every finite output stage is simultaneously certified with probability at least $1-\delta$.

Conditional on $\mathcal F_t$, the $s_t\ge1$ test vectors are iid $N(0,I_n)$, independent of the data used to choose $R_t$
$U_t=\alpha_t\sqrt{2/\pi}\max_{j\le s_t}\|R_tg_{tj}\|_2$, $\alpha_t>1$, and $\sum_t\alpha_t^{-s_t}\le\delta$
$\tau$ is a measurable stage index with values in $\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$
results.conclusion: $\mathbb P\{\exists t:\|R_t\|_2>U_t\}\le\delta$, hence $\mathbb P\{\tau<\infty,\ \|R_\tau\|_2>U_\tau\}\le\delta$

results.title: Effective resistance equals incidence leverage; Foster identity
results.informal: For a finite weighted graph, let $B$ be any oriented incidence matrix, $W=\operatorname{diag}(w_e)$ with positive edge weights, $C=W^{1/2}B$, and $L=C^\top C$. The projector $\Pi=CL^\dagger C^\top$ has diagonal $\Pi_{ee}=w_eR_e$, where $R_e=b_e^\top L^\dagger b_e$; consequently $0\le w_eR_e\le1$ and $\sum_e w_eR_e=|V|-c$.

$c$ is the number of connected components, including isolated vertices
$b_e^\top$ is row $e$ of $B$; $R_e=b_e^\top L^\dagger b_e$ is the resistance between the endpoints of that edge
results.conclusion: $\Pi=\operatorname{proj}_{\operatorname{range}C}$, $\Pi_{ee}=w_eR_e\in[0,1]$, and $\sum_e w_eR_e=\operatorname{rank}L=|V|-c$

results.title: Tikhonov regularization: unique solution, SVD filter and stability
results.informal: For any real or complex rectangular $A$ and $\beta>0$, the unique minimizer of $\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\beta\|x\|_2^2$ is $x_\beta=(A^*A+\beta I)^{-1}A^*b=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\frac{\sigma_i}{\sigma_i^2+\beta}v_i u_i^*b$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$. Moreover $x_\beta\to A^\dagger b$ as $\beta\downarrow0$ and $\|x_\beta(b+e)-x_\beta(b)\|_2\le \|e\|_2/(2\sqrt\beta)$. No full-rank assumption on $A$ is needed.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb K^{m\times n}$, $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, $b,e\in\mathbb K^m$

results.conclusion: $x_\beta=(A^*A+\beta I)^{-1}A^*b$ uniquely minimizes the penalized residual; its SVD filter is $\sigma/(\sigma^2+\beta)$, with the stated limit and noise bound.

results.title: Regularized spectral approximation controls range projection error
results.informal: Let $P$ be the orthogonal projector onto $\operatorname{range}(B)$ and assume $BB^\top+\lambda I\succeq(1-\varepsilon)(AA^\top+\lambda I)$, where $0\le\varepsilon<1$ and $\lambda>0$. Then $I-P\preceq\lambda(BB^\top+\lambda I)^{-1}\preceq\lambda(1-\varepsilon)^{-1}(AA^\top+\lambda I)^{-1}$. Consequently $\|(I-P)A\|_2^2\le\lambda/(1-\varepsilon)$ and $\|(I-P)A\|_F^2\le\lambda d_{\rm eff}^\lambda(A)/(1-\varepsilon)$. For $\varepsilon=1/2$, this yields the spectral bound $2\lambda$ and the Frobenius bound $2(k\lambda+E_k)$.

results.title: Centered error identity for two-sided sketch corrections
results.informal: For $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ and square $L\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$, $R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, set $T=\operatorname{tr}(A^\top AR)+\operatorname{tr}(A^\top LA)-\operatorname{tr}(A^\top LAR)$. Then $T-\|A\|_F^2=-\operatorname{tr}(A^\top(L-I)A(R-I))$. Thus independent random $L,R$ with means $I$ and integrable entries give $\mathbb ET=\|A\|_F^2$.

results.informal: Let $A\succ0$, let B have full row rank m, and put $K=\begin{bmatrix}A&B^*\\B&0\end{bmatrix}$ and $S=BA^{-1}B^*\succ0$. results.title: Rational matrix functions: block differences and Fréchet derivatives
results.informal: Upper triangular block evaluation gives exact finite differences and derivatives of rational matrix functions, including ordered second differences needed for resolvent comparison.
hypotheses: $A,B,C,G,H\in\mathbb C^{d\times d}$; $f=P/Q$ with complex polynomials and $Q(A),Q(B),Q(C)$ invertible

Evaluate $f(M)=P(M)Q(M)^{-1}$ on the full matrix algebra. Define $\Delta f(A,B)[H]$ as the (1,2) block of $f(\begin{smallmatrix}A&H\\0&B\end{smallmatrix})$ and $\Delta^2 f(A,B,C)[G,H]$ as the (1,3) block of $f(\begin{smallmatrix}A&G&0\\0&B&H\\0&0&C\end{smallmatrix})$.
results.conclusion: The first difference is linear and the second is bilinear in the direction matrices. They satisfy $f(A)-f(B)=\Delta f(A,B)[A-B]$, $Df(A)[H]=\Delta f(A,A)[H]$, and $D^2f(A)[G,H]=\Delta^2f(A,A,A)[G,H]+\Delta^2f(A,A,A)[H,G]$. Moreover $\Delta f(A,B)[H]-\Delta f(A,C)[H]=\Delta^2f(A,B,C)[H,B-C]$ and $\Delta f(A,C)[H]-\Delta f(B,C)[H]=\Delta^2f(A,B,C)[A-B,H]$. For $R_\zeta(M)=(\zeta I-M)^{-1}$, $\Delta^2R_\zeta(A,B,C)[G,H]=R_\zeta(A)G R_\zeta(B)H R_\zeta(C)$.

hypotheses: $d,n\ge1$, $S_1,\ldots,S_n$ are independent Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices with finite third moments, $X=\sum_iS_i$, and $S_i'$ are independent copies

results.title: Sample covariance lower bound from fourth moments alone
results.informal: Directional fourth-moment control ensures that an untruncated sample covariance preserves every direction from below, without requiring a bounded vector norm.
hypotheses: $d\ge2$; $w\in\mathbb R^d$ is centered with finite fourth moments and positive definite covariance $K=\mathbb Eww^\mathsf T$
$\beta\ge1$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}(\langle w,a\rangle^2)\le\beta^2(\mathbb E\langle w,a\rangle^2)^2$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$
$w_1,\ldots,w_n$ are independent copies, $\widehat K=n^{-1}\sum_iw_iw_i^\mathsf T$, $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$ and $n\ge26\beta^2\max\{d,\log(d/\delta)\}/\varepsilon^2$
results.conclusion: $\mathbb P\{(1-\varepsilon)K\preceq\widehat K\}\ge1-\delta$.
results.notes: Audit: whiten by K^(-1/2), which explains the explicit positive-definiteness hypothesis from the section's standing setup. The centered rank-one summands have lower eigenvalue at least -1/n regardless of ||w||. Their Gaussian proxy has quadratic-form weak variance <=beta^2/n. A sphere-net argument bounds E||Z|| <=sqrt(12 beta^2 d/n): use a 1/8-net of size <=17^d and the 4/3 quadratic-form norm factor. Apply the lower comparison to obtain error a+sqrt(2s(beta^2+a/3)/n)+s/(3n), where a=sqrt(12 beta^2 d/n) and s=log(d/delta). Under the displayed sample size its three terms are at most 53 epsilon/78, 24 epsilon/78 and epsilon/78, respectively; 53^2>=2808 and 24^2>=574 verify the constants. The displayed probability event in the source's proof has the inequality direction reversed; use the failure event for lambda_min below the threshold, as given by Corollary 1.3. This is a lower spectral guarantee, not two-sided covariance accuracy. Singular covariance can later be handled by restriction to its support. Formalization: the native iid HasLaw theorem proves the literal success probability at least 1-delta, with a companion failure-event theorem and actual product-law versions. It constructs the full-covariance-matched Hermitian Gaussian proxy from the negative centered rank-one summands, derives zero imaginary entries for a proxy of real data, and uses the real-dimensional sphere-net bound without doubling the dimension. The quadratic weak-variance supremum is bounded by beta^2/n from the actual directional fourth moments; no Gaussian norm or variance estimate is supplied as a hypothesis. Positive-definite whitening is performed by an actual invertible inverse-square-root matrix and the original Loewner event is recovered exactly. The exact scalar split 53/78+24/78+1/78=1 proves the displayed constant 26. The checked theorem is stronger than the centered source statement: it works for the positive-definite raw second moment E[ww^T] without requiring E[w]=0. The centered card is obtained directly by retaining its original mean-zero hypothesis. Singular second moments are not included in this capstone.

results.title: Sharp dimension growth for Khatri–Rao embeddings
results.informal: For fixed tensor order $d\ge2$, accuracy and confidence, the worst-case embedding cost of independent isotropic sub-Gaussian tensor-product probes has rank order $r\log^{d-1}(er)$ for factor classes containing the independent-sign witnesses. The upper guarantee is uniform over fixed subspaces and admissible mode dimensions. Explicit independent-sign constructions give the matching obstruction.
hypotheses: $d\ge2$, mode dimensions $n_1,\ldots,n_d$, $r\ge1$ and a deterministic isometry $U:\mathbb R^r\to\bigotimes_j\mathbb R^{n_j}$
The $m$ probe rows are iid tensor products $z_i=\bigotimes_jg_i^{(j)}$; factors are independent and isotropic, with arbitrary coordinate dependence within each factor
$K>0$ and $\mathbb E\exp(\langle u,g^{(j)}\rangle^2/K^2)\le2$ for every unit $u$ and every factor
$0<\varepsilon,\delta<1$, $t=\log(4r/\delta)$ and $\Pi_{i,:}=m^{-1/2}z_i^\top$
results.conclusion: There is a constant $C_{d,K}>0$ such that $m\ge C_{d,K}[rt/\varepsilon^2+(rt^{d-1}+t^d)/\varepsilon]$ implies $\mathbb P\{\Pi\text{ fails to embed }\operatorname{range}(U)\text{ with squared-norm distortion }\varepsilon\}\le\delta$. Conversely, put $k=d-1$, $h=\lfloor\log r/(2k\log2)\rfloor$ and $c_d=[2(4k\log2)^k]^{-1}$. For $r\ge2^{4k}$ the explicit independent-sign construction with mode dimensions $(r,h,\ldots,h)$ has failure probability at least $1-\exp(-\sqrt r)$ for every integer $1\le m\le c_dr(\log r)^k$ and every $\varepsilon<1$. Thus the fixed-parameter rank order is sharp; the lower claim concerns these constructed subspaces, not every subspace or every factor law.

results.title: Irreducible Perron–Frobenius theorem and positive spectral projector
results.informal: An irreducible nonnegative matrix has strictly positive right and left Perron vectors and an algebraically simple Perron root. Its Perron spectral projector is positive and explicitly rank one.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, is entrywise nonnegative, nonzero and irreducible (its directed support graph is strongly connected)
$r=\rho(A)$; normalize right and left Perron vectors by $\sum_i p_i=\sum_i q_i=1$
results.conclusion: $r>0$, $p,q>0$, $Ap=rp$, $A^\top q=rq$, and $r$ has algebraic multiplicity one. Every nonzero nonnegative eigenvector is a positive multiple of the corresponding Perron vector. The spectral projector at $r$ is $P=pq^\top/(q^\top p)>0$.

formalizations.usage: Irreducibility makes every nonzero nonnegative eigenvector strictly positive.
Left and right nonnegative unit-sum Perron vectors are strictly positive for a nonzero irreducible matrix, and its spectral radius is strictly positive.

results.title: Entrywise domination controls the spectral radius
results.informal: Entrywise absolute-value domination controls spectral radii even for a complex matrix. A nonzero entrywise increase strictly raises the spectral radius when the smaller nonnegative matrix is irreducible.

results.title: Collatz–Wielandt variational formulas and Perron root certificates

hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, is entrywise nonnegative
$\alpha(x)=\min_i(Ax)_i/x_i$ and $\beta(x)=\max_i(Ax)_i/x_i$ for $x>0$
results.conclusion: $\alpha(x)\le\rho(A)\le\beta(x)$ for every $x>0$, and $\rho(A)=\inf_{x>0}\beta(x)$. If $A$ is irreducible and nonzero, $\rho(A)=\min_{x>0}\beta(x)=\max_{x>0}\alpha(x)$. For arbitrary $A\ge0$, the support-aware formula is $\rho(A)=\max_{0\ne x\ge0}\min_{i:x_i>0}(Ax)_i/x_i$.

The minimum/maximum ratio certificate for every strictly positive vector.

results.informal: Primitivity is exactly the missing hypothesis that turns irreducible Perron theory into convergence of normalized powers and the nonnegative power method.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, is entrywise nonnegative, nonzero and irreducible; $r=\rho(A)$

For every $0\ne x\ge0$, $A^kx/\sum_i(A^kx)_i\to p$. If $\theta$ is strictly between $\rho(A/r-P)$ and $1$, then $\|(A/r)^k-P\|_2\le C_\theta\theta^k$ for all $k\ge0$ and some finite $C_\theta$.

results.title: Nonsingular M-matrices: inverse positivity, stability and positive scaling

hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, is a Z-matrix: $A_{ij}\le0$ for $i\ne j$

results.title: Regular splittings: inverse positivity is equivalent to convergence
results.informal: A regular splitting converts inverse positivity into a spectral-radius convergence certificate. Consequently every regular splitting of a nonsingular M-matrix converges, and nonnegative data give a monotone iteration from zero.

results.title: Fourier diagonalization of circulants and their singular values

results.title: Circulant least squares and pseudoinverses by Fourier division
results.informal: Fourier coordinates reduce a circulant linear solve or least-squares problem to independent scalar divisions. Setting reciprocal zero modes to zero gives the Moore–Penrose inverse and the minimum-norm least-squares solution.

results.title: Radix-2 FFT: exact DFT realization and arithmetic-operation count
results.informal: The even–odd butterfly recurrence computes the existing DFT exactly. For a length $2^s$ input it uses at most $(n/2)s$ complex multiplications and $ns$ complex additions/subtractions, when roots of unity are supplied as constants.

results.conclusion: This recurrence returns $F_nx$, with $F_{jk}=\omega_n^{jk}$. results.title: Hankel SVD and ERA recover a minimal realization up to similarity
results.informal: Finite Hankel matrices of exact Markov parameters factor as observability times controllability. If this factorization has full state rank, the untruncated ERA formulas reconstruct the original system up to an invertible change of coordinates and reproduce every Markov parameter.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb K^{n\times n}$, $B\in\mathbb K^{n\times q}$, $C\in\mathbb K^{p\times n}$, $n,p,q\ge1$, and positive block horizons $s,t$
$O_s=[C;CA;\ldots;CA^{s-1}]$, $R_t=[B,AB,\ldots,A^{t-1}B]$, with $\operatorname{rank}O_s=\operatorname{rank}R_t=n$
$H_0=[CA^{i+j}B]_{i<s,j<t}=O_sR_t$, $H_1=[CA^{i+j+1}B]_{i<s,j<t}=O_sAR_t$, and $H_0=U\Sigma V^*$ is its compact rank-n SVD

results.title: DEIM greedy interpolation: no breakdown and a sharp projection factor
results.informal: The greedy DEIM selection produces distinct sampling coordinates and an invertible sampled basis. Its interpolation operator reproduces the chosen subspace and amplifies the orthogonal-projection error by at most the inverse sampled-basis norm.
hypotheses: $U=[u_1,\ldots,u_r]\in\mathbb K^{n\times r}$ has orthonormal columns and $1\le r\le n$

results.title: Nested HSS/HBS bases: exact two-pass matvec and linear storage

Thus $\|Z_G\|_2\overset{\mathrm{law}}=\max_\pi\sqrt{N/d_\pi}\|Z_\pi\|_2$.

results.title: Interlacing families select a leaf below the average largest root

results.title: Near doubly stochasticity certifies rank and capacity
results.informal: A normalized completely positive map has quantitative equivalences between capacity and approximate double stochasticity.
hypotheses: $T(X)=\sum_iA_iXA_i^*$ on $M_n(\mathbb C)$, $n\ge1$, and $\operatorname{cap}(T):=\inf_{X\succ0,\det X=1}\det T(X)$.
$T(I)=I$ or $T^*(I)=I$; $\operatorname{ds}(T):=\|T(I)-I\|_F^2+\|T^*(I)-I\|_F^2$.

hypotheses: $d\ge2$, $N\ge2$; $S_i^N$ are independent uniform $N$-permutations restricted to $\mathbf1_N^\perp$; $u_i$ are free Haar unitaries in the reduced group C*-algebra.

$P\in M_D(\mathbb C)\otimes\mathbb C\langle u,u^*\rangle$ is self-adjoint of degree $q_0\ge1$; $K:=\sup_{V}\|P(V,V^*)\|$, supremum over all unitary tuples in all dimensions; $0<\varepsilon<K-\|P(u,u^*)\|$.
results.conclusion: $\mathbb P\{\|P(S^N,S^{N*})\|\ge\|P(u,u^*)\|+\varepsilon\}\le\frac{CD}{N}(Kq_0\log d/\varepsilon)^8\log(eK/\varepsilon)$, with universal $C$.

results.title: Haar polynomial norm bounds with growing matrix coefficients

hypotheses: Independent Haar $U_i^N\in U(N)$; free Haar $u_i$; $P$ of degree $q_0\ge1$, with $D\times D$ coefficients and $\|P(u,u^*)\|>0$.

results.title: Gaussian Schatten norms are controlled by Euclidean row lengths
results.informal: For a symmetric Gaussian matrix, the Schatten norm and the corresponding norm of its row lengths have comparable tails and expectations.
hypotheses: $X$ is real symmetric, $X_{ij}=b_{ij}g_{ij}$ for $i\ge j$, with independent standard real Gaussians and symmetric $b_{ij}\ge0$.
results.conclusion: There is universal $C\ge1$ with $\mathbb P\{R_p(X)\ge t\}\le\mathbb P\{\|X\|_{S_p}\ge t\}\le C\mathbb P\{R_p(X)\ge t/C\}$ for $t\ge0$. In particular $\mathbb E R_p(X)\le\mathbb E\|X\|_{S_p}\le C\mathbb E R_p(X)$.
results.notes: Gaussian structure matters; no arbitrary subgaussian two-sided comparison is claimed.

results.title: Sharp Schatten moments for heterogeneous Gaussian entries
results.informal: The row variances and maximal row entries determine the Schatten moments of a symmetric Gaussian matrix up to universal constants.
hypotheses: $X$ is real symmetric, $X_{ij}=b_{ij}g_{ij}$ for $i\ge j$, with independent standard real Gaussians and symmetric $b_{ij}\ge0$.
$2\le p<\infty$; $F_p(b):=(\sum_i(\sum_jb_{ij}^2)^{p/2})^{1/p}+\sqrt p(\sum_i\max_jb_{ij}^p)^{1/p}$.
results.conclusion: $cF_p(b)\le(\mathbb E\|X\|_{S_p}^p)^{1/p}\le CF_p(b)$ for universal $0<c\le C<\infty$.
results.notes: Unnormalized Schatten norm. Constants are uniform in dimension, p and all variance profiles.

results.title: A smaller iid Gaussian matrix dominates all normalized Gram moments
results.informal: Normalized trace moments of a matrix with independent Gaussian-dominated entries are bounded by those of a dimension-matched homogeneous Gaussian matrix.
hypotheses: $X_{ij}=b_{ij}\xi_{ij}$ is real $n\times m$, $n,m\ge1$, $b_{ij}\ge0$; independent symmetric $\xi_{ij}$ satisfy $\mathbb E\xi_{ij}^{2p}\le\mathbb Eg^{2p}$ for every integer $p\ge1$, $g\sim N(0,1)$.
$\sigma_1^2=\max_j\sum_i b_{ij}^2$, $\sigma_2^2=\max_i\sum_j b_{ij}^2$, $\sigma_*^2=\max_{ij}b_{ij}^2$.
$\sigma_*=1$; $Y$ is $\lceil\sigma_1^2\rceil\times\lceil\sigma_2^2\rceil$ with independent $N(0,1)$ entries.
results.conclusion: $\mathbb E[\operatorname{tr}_n(XX^\top)^p]\le\mathbb E[\operatorname{tr}_{\lceil\sigma_1^2\rceil}(YY^\top)^p]$ for every integer $p\ge1$.

hypotheses: $X_{ij}=b_{ij}\xi_{ij}$ is real $n\times m$, $n,m\ge1$, $b_{ij}\ge0$; independent symmetric $\xi_{ij}$ satisfy $\mathbb E\xi_{ij}^{2p}\le\mathbb Eg^{2p}$ for every integer $p\ge1$, $g\sim N(0,1)$.
$\sigma_1^2=\max_j\sum_i b_{ij}^2$, $\sigma_2^2=\max_i\sum_j b_{ij}^2$, $\sigma_*^2=\max_{ij}b_{ij}^2$.
$0<\sigma_1\le\sigma_2$, $\sigma_*>0$, $0\le t\le\sigma_1^{1/3}\sigma_2/\sigma_*^{4/3}$.

results.title: Finite free additive convolution: matrix identity and root barriers
results.informal: Finite free additive convolution preserves real-rootedness, represents an expected characteristic polynomial, and satisfies a subadditive inverse-Cauchy-transform bound.
hypotheses: $p(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ia_ix^{d-i}$ and $q(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ib_ix^{d-i}$ are monic degree-$d$ real-rooted polynomials, $d\ge1$; $p\boxplus_dq:=\sum_{k=0}^d(-1)^kx^{d-k}\sum_{i+j=k}\frac{(d-i)!(d-j)!}{d!(d-k)!}a_ib_j$.
results.conclusion: $p\boxplus_dq$ is real-rooted; if $p=\chi_A,q=\chi_B$ for Hermitian $A,B$ and Haar $U\in U(d)$, then $p\boxplus_dq=\mathbb E\chi_{A+UBU^*}$. For $w>0$, $\mathcal R_{p\boxplus_dq}(w)\le\mathcal R_p(w)+\mathcal R_q(w)$, where $\mathcal R_p(w)=K_p(w)-1/w$ and $K_p$ inverts $p'/(dp)$ above the largest root. Equality holds precisely when $p$ or $q$ is $(x-\lambda)^d$.
results.notes: Expected characteristic polynomial; no spectral-probability guarantee.

results.title: Finite free multiplicative convolution preserves nonnegative roots
results.informal: Finite free multiplicative convolution preserves nonnegative roots and bounds the largest root by the product of the original largest roots.
hypotheses: $p(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ia_ix^{d-i}$ and $q(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ib_ix^{d-i}$ are monic with nonnegative roots, $d\ge1$; $(p\boxtimes_dq)(x):=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ia_ib_i\binom di^{-1}x^{d-i}$.
results.conclusion: $p\boxtimes_dq$ has nonnegative roots and $\operatorname{maxroot}(p\boxtimes_dq)\le\operatorname{maxroot}(p)\operatorname{maxroot}(q)$. For $p=\chi_A,q=\chi_B$, $A,B\succeq0$, and Haar $U\in U(d)$, $p\boxtimes_dq=\mathbb E\chi_{AUBU^*}$.
results.notes: The product AUBU* need not be Hermitian; the identity is for its characteristic polynomial.

results.title: Multivariate Araki–Lieb–Thirring integral inequality
results.informal: An integral over ordered imaginary powers bounds the Schatten norm of a product of positive matrix powers.
hypotheses: $A_1,\ldots,A_k\succeq0$, $1\le p<\infty$, $0<r<1$; $\beta_r(t)=\sin(\pi r)/(2r[\cosh(\pi t)+\cos(\pi r)])$.

results.title: Multivariate Golden–Thompson through an ordered integral
results.informal: An integral over ordered complex-time exponential products bounds the Schatten norm of the exponential of a Hermitian sum.

results.title: A deterministic shifted-QR strategy rapidly decouples a Hessenberg matrix
results.informal: The specified high-degree shifted QR strategy decouples a well-conditioned diagonalizable Hessenberg matrix in logarithmically many strategy iterations.
hypotheses: $H_0\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge2$, is upper Hessenberg and diagonalizable, $\kappa_V(H_0):=\inf_{H_0=V\Lambda V^{-1}}\|V\|_2\|V^{-1}\|_2\le B$, $B\ge1$; $k\in\{2,4,8,\ldots\}$, $k<n$, $0<\delta<1$.

$\operatorname{dec}_\delta$ is the first strategy iteration with some $|(H_t)_{i+1,i}|\le\delta\|H_t\|_2$; $\operatorname{OptRitz}$ returns 2-optimal degree-k Ritz values in cost $T_{\rm Ritz}(k,2,\delta)$ as defined by the source.

results.title: The matrix Dyson solution is a compactly supported matrix Stieltjes transform
results.informal: A holomorphic positive-imaginary solution of the matrix Dyson equation is the Stieltjes transform of a uniquely determined compactly supported positive matrix measure.
hypotheses: $A\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ is Hermitian, $N\ge1$; complex-linear $\mathcal S:M_N\to M_N$ preserves positive semidefinite matrices and is self-adjoint for $\langle R,T\rangle=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(R^*T)$.
$M:\mathbb H\to M_N(\mathbb C)$ is holomorphic, $\operatorname{Im}M(z)\succ0$, and $-M(z)^{-1}=zI-A+\mathcal S[M(z)]$ for every $z\in\mathbb H$.
results.conclusion: There is a unique PSD matrix-valued measure $V$ with $V(\mathbb R)=I$, supported on $[-\kappa,\kappa]$, $\kappa=\|A\|_2+2\|\mathcal S\|_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{op}}^{1/2}$, such that $M(z)=\int(\tau-z)^{-1}V(d\tau)$; the map norm is induced by the matrix spectral norm. Also $\|M(z)\|_2\le1/\operatorname{Im}z$.

results.notes: This target assumes a holomorphic positive-imaginary solution, as in the source; it does not assert existence or uniqueness of the Dyson solution itself, A1/A2 stability, or a random-matrix local law. The checked inverse capstone is stronger than the displayed data-pair assumptions: positivity of the complex-linear map suffices, and Hilbert–Schmidt self-adjointness is not needed once the actual solution is given. The norm of S is the operator norm for the matrix spectral norm, not its normalized Hilbert–Schmidt operator norm. The norm estimate treats nonnormal matrices through imaginary quadratic coercivity. Normalization follows from ‖zM+I‖≤‖A‖‖M‖+‖S‖‖M‖². The support proof works on vertical lines with fixed |Re z| above c>κ: the barrier excludes 2/(c−‖A‖), continuity and 1/y decay choose the small branch, and the imaginary congruence yields the exact O(Im z) bound. results.title: Gaussian domination of finite centered subgaussian series
results.informal: A finite independent centered subgaussian series in any real normed space has expected norm at most ten times its exponential-square scale times the corresponding Gaussian-series expectation. The comparison also holds with any deterministic affine offset.
hypotheses: $I$ is a finite index set, $E$ is a real normed vector space, $a_i\in E$ and $z\in E$ are deterministic, and $K>0$

$g_i$ are independent standard real Gaussian variables
results.conclusion: $\mathbb E\|\sum_{i\in I}\xi_i a_i\|\le10K\,\mathbb E\|\sum_{i\in I}g_i a_i\|$. More strongly, $\mathbb E\|z+\sum_i\xi_i a_i\|\le\mathbb E\|z+10K\sum_i g_i a_i\|$.

libraries.name: NLAlib (this repo)
libraries.scope: The library this atlas tracks. Layered modules Matrix → Concentration → Gaussian → Sketching → LowRank/Estimation/Krylov → Solvers. NLAlib/Concentration/Matrix/ is Tropp 2015 Ch. 3–8 (formerly the standalone TroppMatrixConcentration project, all Proved on Prove2me), reorganised by topic: Laplace, Series, Chernoff, Bernstein, Intrinsic, OperatorConvexity, Defs. Gaussian/ holds the ported Gaussian Random Matrices series: Concentration/ (integration by parts, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, log-Sobolev, Herbst), Comparison/ (Slepian, Sudakov–Fernique, Gordon minimax), Extreme/ (Lipschitz, Gordon, Chevet, spectral second moment, chi-square, small ball, deviation), InverseMoments/ (inverse Wishart, pseudoinverse tails), Moments/ (fourth moment, approximate multiplication).

libraries.name: Mathlib
libraries.scope: Upstream. Has stdGaussian / multivariateGaussian, HasSubgaussianMGF and the Chernoff-method sum bound, LinearMap.singularValues, the scoped Loewner order on matrices with CFC, Schur complements, matrix exponential, Gamma distribution. Lacks matrix SVD factorization, Eckart–Young, Weyl, Moore–Penrose, chi-square tails, any random matrix theory.

libraries.name: Gaussian Random Matrices I–III (Prove2me)
libraries.scope: Three-mission series in namespace GaussianMatrix on Prove2me (73 accepted solutions). Fully ported into NLAlib/Gaussian/ on 2026-10-09. The Wishart eigenvalue density bound gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral was historically an unproved Prove2me statement; it is now completed locally by the unshifted operator route. Kept for provenance.

libraries.name: LRA (Chen–Persson formalization)
libraries.scope: Local project (~/Documents/Papers/LRA-paper/formal). 253 theorems; RSVD, GN, tGN, etRSVD, etGN proved conditional on explicit Gaussian Props in LRA/Standard/Gaussian.lean.

libraries.name: HighDimProb
libraries.scope: External. Hoeffding, Bernstein, Hanson–Wright with explicit constant 1/(256e²) stated on Mathlib's HasSubgaussianMGF and iIndepFun, covering numbers, Dudley chaining, a Matrix Bernstein route, sample covariance. Pinned to Lean v4.29.1 and reported failing to build on v4.31–v4.33, so it cannot be a lake dependency of the Prove2me-pinned projects; treat as a proof quarry to port from.
